column1: # UNGRADABLE.tsv -- spitbol_testpgms: the lockdown bucket. MIRRORS OUTSIDE_SPITBOL_BASELINE.tsv beside it
# ROW FOR ROW; the runner compares the two every run and says so aloud when they drift. That file is THE
# RECORD and carries the source check; this one is what keeps the four inventory numbers summing to shipped.
# ⛔ Every reason here is ORACLE-SIDE ONLY. lib_inventory.sh REFUSES(2) a reason that names our own compiler,
# because being unable to grade something is a statement about us and never a property of the program -- and
# it reads the WHOLE FILE, comments included, so even a rule cited by title can trip it if the title carries
# that name. Cite such rules by description.

column3: does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 214 -- bad label or misplaced continuation line, test2.spt(238); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 238 `.                                                          ERROR()` -- a lone period in the label column as a continuation marker; SPITBOL reads column 1 as a label and rejects the line before the program runs. ⛔ NONDETERMINISTIC, and this row corrected itself the same hour: a direct sbl -bf run at 2026-09-08 gave ERROR 214 at line 238, so the first draft of this row claimed the refusal was deterministic -- the very next runner pass got rc=231 with no listing instead. One observation is not a determinism claim. Both paths refuse the program and both put it outside the baseline, which is why the classification is stable even though the symptom is not.

does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 116 -- inappropriate file specification for input, test4.spt(65); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 65 `INPUT(.INPUT,,72)` -- a three-argument INPUT association with an EMPTY file specification and a record length; legal SNOBOL4, but SPITBOL requires a real file argument, so it refuses the association rather than the program's logic.

does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 116 -- inappropriate file specification for input, test5.spt(6); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo): stmt 6 `INPUT(.INPUT,,72)` -- the same empty-file-spec association as test4, at the top of the program. Previously graded against a second oracle under CEO-281 clause (2); CEO-391 retires that second oracle, so SPITBOL's refusal is now the whole answer.

does not run in SPITBOL: ERROR 248 -- attempted redefinition of system function, test6.spt(16); source checked 2026-09-08 (coo), REASON CORRECTED 2026-09-13 (ceo CEO-725) after probing the oracle directly rather than reading the line: stmt 16 `DATA('ITEM(COUNT,TOP)')` -- the collision is THE DATA TYPE NAME `ITEM`, which is itself a SPITBOL builtin, and NOT the generated accessors. Measured on sbl -bf: DATA('FOO(COUNT,TOP)') is ACCEPTED, so COUNT and TOP collide with nothing; DATA('ITEM(CNT,TP)') with no colliding field names at all still raises 248. The earlier reason named the wrong half of the statement and stood for five days. ⛔ NOT AN ORACLE REFUSAL EITHER: sbl -bf exits rc=0 on this program -- it runs, dies at statement 4, and prints its own fatal-termination accounting, which is the ORACLE_ACCOUNTING_IN_OUTPUT class (CEO-724). Lon has since ruled all eight programs IN (CEO-725) and named the mechanism: decompose them into the master's one-liner and banner-block entries so each construct is graded on its own.
